development_modes.decision_summary: Base44 direct-to-CloudBOS mode is a useful limited governed client. Git-attached Base44 with project-local .bos, Git authority, Codex Base44 plugin stored-source readback and independent browser acceptance is the full orchestrated-development configuration.

modes.plain_language_outcome: Use CloudBOS guidance and Base44-native building when a local project runtime is not attached.
can_do: Capture public-safe decision and requirement candidates
Generate Base44 entities, functions and UI
Produce provisional platform receipts and runtime evidence
limitations: Cannot independently maintain or promote canonical project .bos and DevPack state
Cannot inspect a local Git worktree, Docker runtime or other deployment environment
Cannot independently accept its own implementation or receipt claim
modes.canonical_memory: Public-safe projection and provisional receipt candidates only
modes.verification: Base44 runtime evidence remains provisional until reconciled through an independent project-authority path.
modes.recommended_for: Early direct builds, Base44-native work and projects without a connected local/Git governance runtime.

modes.plain_language_outcome: Use Base44 for platform-native work while project-local BOS, Git and Codex retain canonical memory and independent acceptance.
can_do: Maintain one canonical Local Development Pack (LDP), including the project model, DevPack and BuildPack
Route each bounded package to Codex or Base44
Verify exact commits and diffs through Git or GitHub
Verify exact post-sync Base44 stored source through the Codex Base44 plugin when available
Verify publication through Base44 owner controls and live behavior through browser road-testing
Test Docker, portability and other target environments
Promote verified evidence into canonical project state
limitations: Requires a connected Git repository and project-local BOS runtime
Allows only one mutating builder per project at a time
The Base44 plugin cannot prove a Git SHA, initiate GitHub sync or publish the app
Publishing and release approval remain separate owner-controlled actions
modes.canonical_memory: Project-local LDP: .bos, DevPack, BuildPack, ./bos and verified receipts
modes.verification: Codex refreshes the exact Git result, computes the actual diff, runs relevant checks, verifies Base44 stored source through the plugin when available, then keeps owner publication and live browser acceptance as separate evidence stages.
modes.recommended_for: Full orchestrated development, multi-environment applications and defensible long-running projects.

unsupported_mode.reason: A hosted Base44 app cannot run the local DBPP compiler, filesystem integrity checks, Git safety checks or independent acceptance loop.

shared_invariants: Application databases, document stores and user records are not synchronised by Git or the governance bridge.
Base44 chat completion text and self-issued receipts are not independent acceptance evidence.
Codex Base44 plugin stored-source readback is independent source evidence but is not Git SHA, publication, live-runtime or security authority.
Only the builder named by the active package route may mutate the same project.
CloudBOS and Base44 receive public-safe projections rather than private project governance internals.
The owner controls build approval, publication, release and any expansion of external authority.

capability_access_model.boundary: Compatibility, maturity and entitlement are independent. Installed BOS files do not prove a paid entitlement.

experimental_capability_policy.plain_language_outcome: Try selected Building Zone capabilities in a controlled runtime pilot before they become fully supported BOS capabilities.
experimental_capability_policy.promotion_boundary: Experimental use produces evidence but never promotes a capability automatically. Canonical installation still requires owner approval and verified readback.

discovery_policy.rule: Surface at most one relevant BOS feature suggestion when a user prompt clearly matches a capability group. Keep it playful and useful, not spammy.
discovery_policy.less_obvious_rule: If the match is plausible but uncertain, ask whether the user wants BOS to handle it once or remember the phrasing for this project.
discovery_policy.ambiguity_guard_rule: Before mutation, detect likely synonym drift and underspecified build intentions such as 'BOS central', 'update the button', 'fix the page', or 'improve the scan'. Proceed with a stated assumption only when recent context clearly identifies the target; otherwise ask one focused clarification question.
discovery_policy.privacy_boundary: Use category-level prompt patterns only. Do not store raw prompts, customer records, secrets, source code, logs, screenshots, or private project data.

dgs_plain_language_activation.boundary: Advisory by default; hard-block only when higher authority or severe DGS risk blocks.
dgs_plain_language_activation.expected_response: Name surface + user goal, apply smallest DGS/Q-DGS check, then proceed safely or ask one focused clarification.

ambiguity_guard.high_confidence_rule: Proceed with a short stated assumption when recent context clearly identifies the target.
ambiguity_guard.clarification_rule: Ask one focused question before mutation when a phrase may refer to more than one BOS surface, feature, page, button, flow, scan, or build intention.

synonym_examples.phrase_pattern: BOS central | central BOS | main BOS
synonym_examples.preferred_question: When you say BOS central, do you mean masterBOS, Cloud BOS, or this app's local BOS files?
I am treating .bis as a typo for .BOS/.bos. Is that what you mean?
synonym_examples.correction_rule: Never create or route to a .bis layer. Use canonical .BOS in owner-facing language and .bos for filesystem paths.

keyboard_proximity_typo_guard.scope: dot-prefixed BOS-like governance terms and owner-facing BOS surface names
keyboard_proximity_typo_guard.rule: When an unrecognized short letter sequence differs from a canonical BOS term by one or two adjacent keyboard keys, treat it as a likely typo, not a new surface.
keyboard_proximity_typo_guard.mutation_rule: Before mutation, correct the term or ask one focused question; never create a new file, layer, route, capability, or memory entry from the typo.
